### Added
- **agent-manager's session tools reach the kagent controller: `agent-manager.kagent.controllerTarget` is derived, and agent-manager's egress admits the agentgateway data plane** (giantswarm/agent-manager#3). With the kagent and agentgateway components on and `kagent.controllerRoute.enabled`, the target is `grpc://<gateway.name>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:<gateway.listeners[0].port>` (`grpc://agentgateway.agent-platform.svc.cluster.local:8080` on a default install); with the route off it is empty, which turns `list_sessions`, `get_session` and `start_session` off. A differing `agent-manager.kagent.controllerTarget` fails the render naming the key. `components.agent-manager.versionRange` is `>=1.10.0 <2.0.0` (the floor the migrate entry below sets): 1.10.0 is the first agent-manager release whose schema takes `kagent.controllerTarget` (giantswarm/agent-manager#101), so a BOM that pins agent-manager pins 1.10.0 or later (`examples/customer-bom.yaml` does). With agent-manager's OAuth on and the route on, its network policy (both flavors) admits the data plane on the listener port.
### Changed
- **The agentgateway line moves to 2.3.0 (controller and data plane), and `llmRouting.modelCatalog.providers` is empty by default in both charts.** 2.3.0's built-in catalog prices `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` at the rates the overlay carried, so the overlay entry is dropped (`make verify-model-catalog` refuses an overlay that shadows the gateway's own catalog); cost attribution for that model is unchanged. An installation that sets its own `providers` keeps them. The line dropped its fork patch for oversized MCP answers in 2.2.2 (agentgateway#3714 was declined upstream and the carry reverted in giantswarm/agentgateway-upstream#36), so an MCP answer above the gateway's buffer is reported as upstream's `body exceeded buffer limit` / `length limit exceeded` again instead of the named buffer error.
- **The connectivity chart's `agent-manager migrate` run moves the agents from Generic chart 1.x to 2.x, and `components.agent-manager.versionRange` is `>=1.10.0 <2.0.0` (was `>=1.7.0 <2.0.0`), `agentManager.migration.image.tag` `1.10.0` (was `1.7.0`), in both charts.** agent-manager 1.10.0 reads the 2.x range of `agent-manager.agentChart.semver` as the 1.x to 2.x path (giantswarm/agent-manager#100): every Generic-chart release is validated against the chart 2.x schema, the writable ones are rewritten (sub-agent bindings to `subAgent`, the 1.x Harness admission label to `agent.harness`) and their namespace's `OCIRepository agent` moves to 2.x, GitOps-owned releases and sources get a diff in the report, and the leftover `kagent.dev` AgentTemplates are deleted once the Agents are Ready. An older image read the same range as the 0.x to 1.x path and rewrote nothing. The run deletes no CRD, so its ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding on the five `kagent.dev` CRDs of the 0.x line are gone: the migration holds no cluster-scoped right (`make verify-identity` asserts none renders). `AGENT_CHART_SEMVER` falls back to `2.x`.
- **`components.kagent-crds.ownedCrds` is `[modelconfigs.api.kagent.dev]` (was `[modelconfigs.kagent.dev]`)**: the one-owner guard looks up the CRD the kagent-crds chart on the `api.kagent.dev` line installs.
- **`agent-manager.agentChart.semver` is `>=2.0.0 <3.0.0` (was `>=1.5.0 <2.0.0`)**: the Generic agent chart 2.x renders one `api.kagent.dev/v1alpha3` `Agent` (giantswarm/agent#56) in place of the `kagent.dev` AgentTemplate, which the kagent line on `api.kagent.dev` no longer serves; every agent namespace's OCIRepository follows and the agents re-render as Agents.
- **`components.model-manager.versionRange` is `>=1.14.0 <2.0.0` (was `>=1.10.2 <2.0.0`), in both charts** (giantswarm/model-manager#247). 1.14.0 writes its ModelConfigs at `api.kagent.dev` when the cluster serves it: a bare `kagent.apiVersion` (the platform's `v1alpha3`) keeps the version and discovers the group, re-checked every minute and at once on a NotFound, so the served models stay listed for the agents after the cut-over; an older model-manager keeps writing `kagent.dev`, which the line's agents do not read.
- **`components.kagent{,-crds}.versionRange` is `>=1.4.0 <1.5.0` and `components.substrate{,-crds}.versionRange` is `>=1.5.0 <1.6.0`: the kagent line on upstream `bf8afa56` (`api.kagent.dev/v1alpha3`, Agents and Sessions) and the Substrate release it was built against.** kagent 1.4.0 fences a session's Pause and Suspend with a Substrate lease token (giantswarm/kagent-upstream#216), which Substrate takes from 1.5.0 (giantswarm/substrate#182); Substrate 1.5.0 also gives the carried `ExternalSnapshot` source field its own number and rewrites the rows a 1.3 or 1.4 release wrote when it reads them (giantswarm/substrate#165), so an Actor paused under the 1.3 line resumes on this one. The kagent WorkerPool's worker image follows the Substrate floor to `ateom-gvisor:1.5.0`. The cut-over of an installation is `docs/kagent-v1alpha3-cutover.md` (a fresh kagent database; every session is lost).
- **The kagent catalog is `api.kagent.dev/v1alpha3`: the connectivity chart's ModelConfigs and RemoteMCPServers, the LLM routing admission policy's `modelconfigs` rule and the CRD validation (`make verify-kagent-crds`) move to the group the re-pinned kagent line serves** (kagent-dev/kagent#2952). The line renders explicit `Agent`s: the Generic agent chart renders one `Agent` per release with its template inline and its Harness by name (`spec.harnessRef`), and the display-name and icon annotations are read off the `Agent`. The kagent controller GRPCRoute (`kagent.controllerRoute.grpc.services`) carries `kagent.api.v1alpha1.AgentService` and `kagent.api.v1alpha1.SessionService` in place of `AgentInstanceService`, next to `AgentTemplateService`, `ModelService`, `SystemService` and `lf.a2a.v1.A2AService`; kagent's MCP server on muster offers `list_sessions` and `invoke_session`. The ModelConfig helpers admit the `Mistral` provider the line's CRD adds, with its `mistral.baseUrl` block. The floors of `components.kagent.versionRange` and `components.kagent-crds.versionRange` move to the first release of the re-pinned kagent line once it is tagged; until then the range admits the 1.2.x line, and `make verify-kagent-crds` runs against the candidate's CRDs through `KAGENT_CRDS_DIR`.
- **The platform Harness has no admission selector: `kagent.harness` forwards `create`, the snapshot location, the env and the compaction alone.** The line's Harness CRD (`api.kagent.dev`) has no `allowedAgentTemplates`; an `Agent` names its Harness by `spec.harnessRef` and the label `agent-platform.giantswarm.io/harness` means nothing to the platform any more. `kagent.controller.auth.mode` is `insecure` or `trusted-proxy` on the line (the chart renders it as `KAGENT_AUTH_MODE`; the platform's default `trusted-proxy` is unchanged, and the retired spelling `unsecure` is gone from the comments). The line's session lifecycle knobs (`kagent.controller.sessionIdleTTL`, `sessionShareMaxTTL`, `stalledTurnTimeout`, `pausedRuntimeTTL`) travel as written; the platform sets none. `make verify-kagent-harness` and `make verify-meta` assert the forwarded block, and `make verify-components-charts` asserts the rendered Harness carries no selector, which holds once the range resolves to the re-pinned line. The ATS suites apply a declarative `Agent` and wait on the `Agent`'s `Ready` condition.
- **The line starts on a fresh kagent database; nothing migrates from 1.x.** The re-pinned kagent line rewrites its initial schema (`000001_initial.sql`) for the Session baseline and does not migrate a 1.x database: a controller of the line pointed at one refuses to start before any migration, with `KAGENT_SKIP_MIGRATIONS` too. An installation cuts over the way the API v2 cut-over did (giantswarm/agent-platform#346): a new CNPG `Database` in `postgres.databases` for the controller, the 1.x database kept as it is for a retention period and dropped afterwards, together with the Substrate ActorTemplates, golden snapshots, parked Actors and snapshot-store checkpoints its rows reference. The fresh database does not carry conversations and their history, session shares (the klaus-gateway thread bindings that point at them), scheduled-run executions or the sessions' checkpoints; Agents, templates and schedules are Kubernetes objects and are recompiled on the first reconcile. `docs/kagent-v1alpha3-cutover.md` is the per-installation checklist.
- **The agentgateway policies hold on the re-pinned agentgateway line (upstream main at c9573ed1).** Checked against the three upstream changes the line carries: no `AgentgatewayPolicy` of either chart reads `backend.endpoint` in CEL (agentgateway/agentgateway#3679 removes it for Service backends); the one transformation the charts render sets the `x-user-id` request header on the kagent controller route from the verified JWT claim and touches no body, so the null-body change (agentgateway/agentgateway#3653: a null body expression keeps the upstream body) changes nothing here; and the `llm` path fronts Anthropic only by default (`llmRouting.models`: provider `Anthropic`, `https://api.anthropic.com/v1`), whose Messages input passes through untranslated, while agentgateway/agentgateway#3647 makes an `llm` backend translate Anthropic Messages to OpenAI Responses first and Completions second. An installation that adds a Completions-only OpenAI-compatible provider to `llmRouting.models` and sends it Anthropic Messages sets `AGENTGATEWAY_MESSAGES_PREFER_COMPLETIONS=true` on the data plane (`gateway.parameters.dataPlaneEnv`) until it serves the Responses API; upstream drops the switch in v1.7. A served model behind `LLMEndpoint` answers whichever API its runtime exposes and is unaffected. The floor of `components.agentgateway.versionRange` moves to the first release of the re-pinned agentgateway line once it is tagged.
- **The Substrate values are ready for the re-pinned Substrate line (kagent-dev/substrate v0.3.0-alpha1 plus the carried patches).** Every key the meta chart forwards to the substrate release keeps its name and shape there (`credentialProvider.namespacePolicies`, `postgres`, `rustfs`, `otel`, `podLabels`, `images`, `atelet.*`, `metrics.podMonitor`), so no value changes. What the line changes underneath: `ate-controller` and `ate-api-server` name the atelet and router ServiceAccounts (`--atelet-service-account`, `--router-service-account`), the router names its Service (`--router-service-name`), the credential provider serves a status endpoint on 4040 (`--status-address`; its probes stay on the metrics port, so the network policies are unchanged) and names the egress injector with `--injector-identity`, its credential URIs are `ate-secret://k8s.io/default/<namespace>/<secret>/<key>` (`uriAuthority: k8s.io`; the charts render none), atelet tolerates the `ate.dev/sandboxClass` taint itself, and a microvm `SandboxConfig` no longer needs a `kata-config` asset (the platform runs gVisor). `substrate.images.agentgateway` is not forwarded: the atenet router and egress run the agentgateway build the Substrate release stamps (2.2.1 on alpha1), which moves with the Substrate release, not with this chart. The floors of `components.substrate.versionRange` and `components.substrate-crds.versionRange` move to the first release of the re-pinned Substrate line once it is tagged; until then the range admits the 1.1.x line.
### Removed
- **`kagent.harness.allowedAgentTemplates` and `kagent.controller.substrate.defaultWorkerPool`.** The re-pinned kagent line's Harness has no selector and its chart no `defaultWorkerPool` key (every ActorTemplate is pinned to the pool of the Harness the Agent names). An installation that set either removes it from its values; an `AgentTemplate` labelled `agent-platform.giantswarm.io/harness: kagent` is not admitted by the label any more, it needs an `Agent` that names the Harness.
- **The kagent CRDs' storage-version hooks of the 3.x → 4.x cut-over** (giantswarm/agent-platform#396): `<release>-kagent-storage-version-backup` and `-restore`, `make verify-kagent-storage-version`. The kagent line serves `api.kagent.dev`, and the `kagent.dev` CRDs the hooks moved from `v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3` leave the cluster with the kagent-crds release that stops rendering them; the restore hook waited on `modelconfigs.kagent.dev` and would have failed every upgrade after the cut-over. With the engine off the meta chart renders no hook, no hook identity and no hook policy (a pure app-of-apps render; the serving slice's teardown aside); with the engine on the hook identity is at `pre-install,pre-upgrade,pre-delete,post-delete`. An installation still on 3.x upgrades through a 4.x release that carries the hooks first (UPGRADE.md).
